q: What is Azure DNS?
opts: A hosting service for DNS zones that resolves names using Microsoft's global name servers
exp: Azure DNS hosts public and private zones.

q: Which CLI command creates a public DNS zone for contoso.com?
opts: az network dns zone create -g RG1 -n contoso.com
exp: az network dns zone create creates a public zone.

q: Which CLI command adds an A record 'www' → 20.1.2.3 in zone contoso.com?
opts: az network dns record-set a add-record -g RG1 -z contoso.com -n www -a 20.1.2.3
az network dns add www A
exp: Record-set commands manage records by type.

q: Which record type maps a name to another name (an alias), for example www → contoso.azurewebsites.net?
exp: CNAME maps one name to another.

q: Which record type directs email for a domain to mail servers?
exp: MX records specify mail exchangers.

q: Can a CNAME record set contain more than one record?
opts: No — CNAME record sets can hold only one record
exp: A CNAME set has a single record, and CNAMEs aren't allowed at the apex.

q: You need to delegate subdomain dev.contoso.com to a separate Azure DNS zone. What do you add in the parent zone contoso.com?
opts: An NS record set 'dev' with the child zone's name servers
exp: Child zone delegation uses NS records in the parent.

q: What's the effect of a lower TTL on a DNS record?
opts: Resolvers cache the record for less time, so changes propagate faster but query volume rises
exp: TTL controls caching duration.

q: How do you prevent accidental deletion of a production DNS zone and its records?
opts: Apply a CanNotDelete resource lock on the zone (record sets can also be protected)
exp: Resource locks protect DNS zones from deletion.

q: Which RBAC role lets a user manage records in a DNS zone without changing other resources?
exp: DNS Zone Contributor manages zones and records.

q: How can you check that delegation to Azure DNS works?
opts: Run nslookup -type=SOA contoso.com and confirm Azure name servers answer
exp: Use nslookup or dig to verify NS/SOA responses.

q: Which alias record target types does Azure DNS support?
opts: Public IP addresses, Traffic Manager profiles, Azure Front Door/CDN endpoints, and other record sets in the same zone
exp: Alias records point to Azure resources and record sets.

q: Which CLI command links a private DNS zone to VNet1 with auto-registration?
opts: az network private-dns link vnet create -g RG1 -z contoso.local -n link1 -v VNet1 -e true
exp: -e true (registration-enabled) turns on auto-registration.

q: How many private DNS zones can a VNet be linked to with auto-registration enabled?
exp: A VNet can have only one registration-enabled private zone link.

q: VMs in VNet1 and VNet2 (peered) must resolve each other's names through private zone corp.local. What do you do?
opts: Link corp.local to both VNets (registration enabled on each, if desired)
exp: Private zones resolve only for linked VNets; peering doesn't share DNS.

q: On-premises servers must resolve names in an Azure private DNS zone without deploying DNS VMs. Which service?
exp: Private Resolver inbound endpoints accept queries from on-premises.

q: Azure VMs must resolve names in an on-premises domain (corp.contoso.com). Which Private Resolver components?
opts: An outbound endpoint plus a DNS forwarding ruleset linked to the VNet
exp: Outbound endpoints and rulesets forward queries to on-premises DNS.

q: Answer Yes or No:
stmts: Private DNS zones are resolvable from the internet
A private DNS zone can be linked to VNets in different regions
Auto-registration creates records for VMs' private IPs
A private zone name can match a public domain name (split-horizon)
exp: Private zones are internal; links work across regions; auto-registration records private IPs; split-horizon is supported.

q: What are the main components of Azure Load Balancer?
opts: Frontend IP, backend pool, health probe, load-balancing rules
exp: Those four components define LB behavior.

q: Which CLI command creates a Standard public load balancer?
opts: az network lb create -g RG1 -n lb1 --sku Standard --public-ip-address pip1 --frontend-ip-name fe1 --backend-pool-name be1
exp: az network lb create sets the SKU, frontend, and backend pool.

q: What are the default health probe settings commonly used for an HTTP probe?
opts: Interval 5 seconds, path such as /health on port 80
exp: Probes can be TCP, HTTP, or HTTPS; HTTP probes check a path and expect 200 OK.

q: An HTTP health probe on /health returns 302 (redirect). What's the probe result?
opts: Unhealthy — HTTP probes need a 200 status
exp: Any status other than 200 marks the instance down.

q: Which protocols does Azure Load Balancer support in load-balancing rules?
opts: TCP and UDP (or All with HA ports)
exp: It's a Layer 4 load balancer.

q: Which resources can be in a Standard load balancer's backend pool?
opts: VMs or VMSS instances (by NIC or IP address) in a single VNet
exp: Backend pools contain NIC- or IP-based members within one VNet.

q: VMs behind a Standard internal load balancer have no outbound internet access. Why?
opts: Standard internal LBs don't provide outbound SNAT; add a NAT Gateway or another explicit outbound method
exp: Internal Standard LB backends need an explicit outbound path.

q: What does the Floating IP (direct server return) option on a load-balancing rule do?
opts: Preserves the frontend IP as the destination in packets delivered to the backend, for scenarios like SQL Always On listeners
exp: Floating IP is needed for some clustering scenarios.

q: What's the default idle timeout for TCP flows on Azure Load Balancer, and can it change?
exp: The idle timeout defaults to 4 minutes and can go up to 100. TCP reset on idle can be enabled.

q: What's the purpose of an outbound rule on a public Standard load balancer?
opts: Explicitly configure outbound SNAT for backend VMs (public IPs, allocated ports)
exp: Outbound rules control SNAT for backend outbound connections.

q: Which load balancer distributes traffic across regions at Layer 4 using a global frontend IP?
exp: The cross-region LB fronts regional Standard LBs.

q: Order the steps to load-balance web traffic across two VMs with a public Standard LB:
items: Create a load-balancing rule (TCP 80, frontend → backend pool, probe)
Create the LB with a Standard public IP frontend
Add the VMs' NICs to the backend pool and create a health probe
Allow port 80 in the VMs' NSGs
exp: LB → pool and probe → rule → NSG.

q: Which TWO conditions cause a Standard LB to send no traffic to a backend VM?
opts: The NSG doesn't allow the traffic
The VM has a Premium SSD
The VM is in an availability zone
exp: A probe failure removes the VM from rotation; a missing NSG allow drops traffic.

q: The health probe shows all backends down, but the app works locally on the VMs. What should you check?
opts: That the app listens on the probe port/path and that the guest firewall or NSG doesn't block the AzureLoadBalancer source (168.63.129.16)
exp: Probes come from 168.63.129.16 and must reach the probe port.

q: A backend VM can't reach the load balancer's own frontend IP (hairpin), but external clients can. Why?
opts: A backend instance connecting to its own LB frontend isn't supported when the flow lands on itself (hairpinning)
exp: Azure Load Balancer doesn't support hairpinning to the same backend.

q: Which Load Balancer metric shows whether backend instances are passing health probes?
exp: Health Probe Status shows per-backend probe health; Data Path Availability shows frontend health.

q: Intermittent outbound connection failures appear from VMs behind a load balancer under heavy load. Likely cause and fix?
opts: SNAT port exhaustion; use a NAT Gateway or allocate more outbound IPs/ports
exp: SNAT exhaustion limits concurrent outbound connections.

q: Which Azure Monitor experience gives a topology and metrics dashboard for a load balancer?
exp: Insights provides a dependency view and metrics.

q: Which Application Gateway feature routes requests for api.contoso.com and www.contoso.com to different backend pools?
exp: Multi-site listeners route by host header.

q: Application Gateway needs which subnet setup?
opts: A dedicated subnet for the gateway
exp: Application Gateway needs its own dedicated subnet; GatewaySubnet is for VPN/ExpressRoute.

q: Which Application Gateway feature protects apps from SQL injection and cross-site scripting?
opts: Web Application Firewall (WAF) with OWASP rule sets
exp: The WAF uses managed OWASP/CRS rules.

q: Which service load-balances globally by DNS (priority, weighted, performance, geographic routing)?
exp: Traffic Manager is DNS-based global routing.

q: A global web app needs edge TLS termination, caching, a WAF, and fast failover between regions at Layer 7. Which service?
exp: Front Door is a global Layer 7 edge service.

q: Internal non-HTTP traffic (TCP 1433) must be distributed across SQL VMs inside a VNet. Choose:
exp: Use an internal Layer 4 balancer for TCP inside a VNet.

q: Which combination gives zone-redundant Layer 4 load balancing for VMs spread across 3 zones?
opts: Standard LB with a zone-redundant frontend and backend VMs in zones 1, 2, 3
Basic LB with an availability set
exp: Standard LB zone-redundant frontends survive zone failures.

q: Answer Yes or No:
stmts: A Standard LB can mix VMs from two different VNets in one backend pool
An inbound NAT rule can map a frontend port range to multiple VMs in a pool
A health probe can use HTTPS
A Basic public IP can be used with a Standard LB
exp: A backend pool is limited to one VNet; inbound NAT rules can target pools with port ranges; HTTPS probes are supported; SKUs must match.

q: Which load balancer type inserts third-party NVAs transparently in the traffic path, chained to a Standard LB frontend?
exp: Gateway LB enables NVA chaining (bump-in-the-wire).

q: An app needs TCP traffic on port 443 balanced to backend port 8443. Is that possible?
opts: Yes — load-balancing rules map a frontend port to a different backend port
exp: Rules define frontend and backend ports separately.

q: Answer Yes or No:
stmts: Azure DNS supports DNSSEC signing for public zones
An alias record can point the apex at a Traffic Manager profile
You can import a zone file into Azure DNS with the CLI
Azure DNS public zones need a VNet link
exp: DNSSEC is supported; apex aliases to Traffic Manager work; zone import is available; public zones aren't linked to VNets.

q: A VMSS behind a Standard LB should send each client to the same instance for 30 minutes. What do you use?
opts: Session persistence (Client IP) on the rule plus a suitable idle timeout
exp: Client IP affinity keeps clients on one instance.

ctx: Requirements: public HTTPS web app in 2 regions, failover between regions, URL path routing (/api to API servers), WAF protection, and an internal TCP service for the API servers' cache layer.
q: Which design best matches?
opts: Front Door (global L7, WAF) → regional Application Gateways (path routing) → internal Standard LB for the cache layer
exp: Use global L7 for failover and WAF, regional App Gateway for paths, and an internal LB for TCP.

ctx: contoso.com is delegated to Azure DNS. The apex has an alias record pointing to pip-lb (Standard public IP of LB1). LB1 has a TCP 80 rule and a health probe on /health. NSG on the VMs allows port 80 from Internet.
q: Answer Yes or No:
stmts: If pip-lb is replaced by a new IP resource, the alias record updates automatically
Clients can reach the app on http://contoso.com if at least one backend probe is healthy
A CNAME could have been used at the apex instead of the alias
If /health returns 500 on all VMs, traffic is still delivered
exp: An alias tracks the referenced resource's IP changes, but replacing the resource with a NEW one means updating the alias target; healthy backends serve traffic; CNAMEs can't be at the apex; all-down probes mean no delivery.
